messages:
sam: Heads up — we're seeing an apparent fleet-wide ECC/Xid surge but the pattern looks... wrong. Multiple racks reporting identical spike shapes at the same second, telemetry lag on NICs is high. auto-drain kicked and we lost ~18% GPU capacity in us-west2 :warning:

tanvi: oncall — pulling logs now. which alert fired first?

sam: gpu.ecc.count spike alert then drain-run triggered by drain-controller. I think the ECC counts are fed by a telemetry pipeline that fell back to buffered aggregation when egress errors hit, so multiple hosts flushed high counters at once.

oliver: Confirming telemetry egress errors on the infra metrics plane across rack-b and rack-c, same timestamp window. nvme/host telemetry shows: 
```
2026-03-18T09:11:02Z host-12 metrics-collector: send failed: connection reset by peer
2026-03-18T09:11:02Z host-42 metrics-collector: enqueue metric batch (size=512)
2026-03-18T09:11:02Z host-42 metrics-collector: flush-success
```

lee: If buffered flushes replayed aggregated ECC deltas we could get bursty spikes. Current risk is unnecessary drains that reduce capacity. We should stop auto-drain until we validate.

sam: Agreed. tanvi can you pause the drain-controller for us-west2 and open a mitigation window?

infra-bot: drain-controller: pause request received for cluster us-west2 by tanvi. Pausing auto-drain for 30m (reason: telemetry-flush-fanout-investigation).

tanvi: done. Also bumped reserved spare pool by +12 GPUs from autoscaling group to cover demand for the next hour.

oliver: quick PromQL used to cross-check aggregation behavior: 
```
sum by(pod) (rate(gpu_ecc_total[1m]))
```
When I plot at 1m vs 10s aggregation you can see the 1m line jumps when buffered batches flush. 10s shows flat normal.

sam: thanks. Any evidence of real hardware errors? run nvml query on a few affected nodes?

lee: ran nvml on three sampled hosts — counters are low and not increasing now. No persistent Xid resets in kernel logs. That points to pipeline accounting hiccup not card flake.

ops-bot: incident-ticket CREATED: https://tickets.internal/INC-2026-789 (title: telemetry flush -> false ECC spike -> inadvertent drains)

tanvi: action plan: 1) keep drains paused 2) maintain +12 spare GPUs until 18:00 UTC 3) rollback recent metrics-collector sidecar image (deployed 2h before spike) on a canary subset 4) add an aggregation-safety filter to drain-controller (ignore >90th percentile flush deltas)

oliver: initiated canary rollback to metrics-collector:v2026-03-16 on 5 hosts in rack-b. Monitoring for repeat spike.

sam: temp observability query suggestion to reduce noisy alerts: 
```
increase(gpu_ecc_total[5m]) > 0 and not (sum_over_time(metrics_egress_errors[5m]) > 5)
```
Only alert on ECC increases if egress errors aren't also elevated.

lee: good. patching drain-controller config now to include that guard, will roll to us-west2 only.

infra-bot: drain-controller: config update applied to us-west2 (guard: skip-if-egress-errors>5).

tanvi: canary rollback succeeded and no spike replayed on the 5 hosts. nvml still normal.

sam: spare pool holding up, customer impact minimal but we should estimate cost delta for the hour.

tanvi: rough numbers: +12 GPUs * 1h ~ $9.6 (on-demand estimate) — not huge. logging it in the ticket.

lee: next steps: schedule a deeper postmortem to confirm root cause (collector batching logic) and follow-up to harden drain-controller; ticket INC-2026-789 assigned to oliver and lee.

sam: thanks team. once postmortem created drop it into the incident channel and link to oncall runbook. :thumbsup:
